newsitem.title: USA: Southwest Airlines rated top in quality survey.
newsitem.headline: Southwest Airlines rated top in quality survey.

text.p: Southwest Airlines Co., for the second year in a row, was named the top U.S. carrier in the annual Airline Quality Rating issued on Monday by two Midwest universities.
It said American Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp., United Airlines, a unit of UAL Corp. and Delta Air Lines Inc. repeated their second, third place and fourth place finishes of 1995.
The rating by the School of Business at Wichita State University and the University of Nebraska at Omaha put Trans World Airlines Inc. last of the nine carriers surveyed.

Ratings are based on factors that include average age of fleet, number of aircraft, on-time performance, number of accidents, denied boardings, mishandled baggage, fares, customer service and the airline's financial stability.
Brent Bowen, director of the Aviation Institute at Omaha, said the first place gap widened since 1995, but there was little difference among the next five carriers.
He told a news conference that Southwest's top rating was due in part because it had stressed on-time performance, resolving complaints and baggage handling.
"Southwest is clearly out there by itself," said Dean Headley, associate professor of marketing at Wichita.
He added that "Continental Airlines is the most improved."
Following the top four carriers were Continental Airlines, Northwest Airlines, US Airways Group Inc. (formerly USAir) America West Airlines and TWA.
Headley said overall quality was up in 1996, but added that while airlines were winners and doing well financially, "the consumers seem to be the losers."
He said this showed up in longer lines at ticket counters and boarding gates.
Headley said that while the annual quality rating included accidents and pilot deviations from prescribed operations, it did not rank carriers on safety.

He said airlines were continuing to work to improve and that accidents in any single year should not be used to judge safety, noting that the accident rate the past five years was down from the previous five years.
Among the points the survey made were:
- American slipped a bit with more consumer complaints and mishandled baggage and a worse on-time performance;
- United also slipped a bit with more mishandled baggage and a lower on-time performance, but had fewer complaints;
- Delta improved in factors that included on-time performance and consumer complaints;
- Continental showed dramatic gains, with the fewest denied boardings of the nine major carriers surveyed, second best in lost baggage rate and a nearly 50 percent drop in consumer complaints;
- TWA scored about the same as in 1995. It had the worst on-time performance, the second worse baggage handling record and the highest rate of consumer complaints.
